mechaber.1#main: The law of birds filled with unsalted meat. In it is one seif: Birds or kids that one fills with meat that was not salted — if for roasting it is permitted even with their mouths upward, and even if the outer part was salted — for as it absorbs the blood of the filling so it releases it: {Rama: And all the more so if the inner part was salted and not the outer — it is permitted (it appears to me according to Arukh general rule 9) for fire draws and absorbs the blood from the outer part and it is not absorbed in the inner (it appears to me).} But for a pot it is forbidden until one salts the outer alone and the inner alone; but if after filling one salted the outer part it does not release the blood in the inner: {Rama: And all this is b'dieved; but l'chatchila one should not make any filling unless both were salted (Agur and Mordechai chapter 25 and Rashi). And all this applies when this filling has only meat or herbs; but if there are eggs that harden, its law is as if it was cooked in a pot (Hagahat ShaDa in the name of Maharit and Arukh and Bach). And even b'dieved one should forbid if both were not salted. Unsalted meat that was not rinsed that was roasted with salted meat that was rinsed is permitted b'dieved (there). But l'chatchila it is forbidden to roast salted meat with unsalted meat even if rinsed:}

siftei-kohen.1#א: ["And even if the outer part was salted, etc. — language of Rosh and Tur: and it remained for the time of salting — now it is not busy to exude, and it is proven that he means even if it remained for the time of salting and was rinsed — then it does not exude even gravy; as explained above siman 70 s.k. 26; and so it is proven from the proof that Tosafot, Rosh, and Mordechai brought from coating of a bar goose — see there and investigate:"]
siftei-kohen.1#ב: ["And all the more so if the inner was salted and not the outer, etc. — view of Rav: even if the inner was salted and remained for the time of salting it does not absorb from the outer, for fire draws and absorbs from the outer and expels — so in Darkei Moshe and Tur HaChadash general rule 9 law 3 from Or Zarua; and in my book I elaborated and proved with clear proofs that all poskim agree that where the inner was salted and remained for the time of salting and the outer is unsalted or did not remain for the time of salting — the inner is forbidden because regarding the inner we do not say as it absorbs so it releases, since it has no blood of its own to exude, and the inner absorbs and we do not say in such a case fire draws to it; but if the inner was not salted it is forbidden only when the outer was salted and did not remain — as Mordechai wrote in the name of R' Yoel and Rabbenu Tam chapter 25 — then the inner absorbs before roasting; and even though we hold above siman 70 that meat salted on unsalted meat — salting afterward helps, and all the more roasting — here it is different since it is inside; and I wrote there that Semak siman 205 and Hagahot Maimoniyot in the name of Tosafot, Beit Yosef, and Rav in Tur HaChadash understood Hagahot Maimoniyot applies where the outer was salted and remained — which is not the case; and moreover Tosafot wrote that in such a case it is permitted, and so implies from the Gemara from what they challenge from coating of bar goose — see there and investigate. And I further proved there that Semak and Hagahot Maimoniyot agree; and Or Zarua beginning general rule 9 also applies in such a case (also I wrote there Mahari Trushan agrees in all these laws — see there); and Rav in Tur HaChadash and Darkei Moshe understood Or Zarua on a different matter — very forced; but when inner equals outer — both salted and remained, or both unsalted, or even both salted and did not remain — permitted in every case as Mordechai states explicitly; but when inner unsalted and outer salted, remained, and rinsed — obviously permitted; and as Taz wrote regarding outer we say as it absorbs so it releases even though it does not exude its own blood; and even though regarding meat salted on already salted rinsed meat we hold above siman 70 salting and roasting afterward do not help — here it is different since it exudes immediately at the time of absorption; therefore if inner salted and did not remain and outer salted, remained, and rinsed — or already exuded all its gravy — the outer is forbidden for it absorbs also from the inner before roasting — all this I brought there to reconcile the poskim and it is clear; and so is Maharshal's view in all this in Or Zarua end gate 4 and in his book chapter of Chullin siman 29 — see there; and as you will find in Maharshal's words that where inner salted and did not remain and outer remained — the outer is permitted — must explain his words that outer was not rinsed and did not exude all its gravy, though somewhat forced in his words, for certainly outer is not better than other meat salted on already salted rinsed meat or that exuded all gravy — forbidden even for roasting as explained above siman 70; and Maharshal also wrote so in several places:"]
siftei-kohen.1#ג: ["Until one salts the outer alone and the inner alone. Explanation: and rinse each separately after salting, for otherwise it is meat cooked without final rinsing which is forbidden — as above siman 69 seif 9; and so other Acharonim explained:"]
siftei-kohen.1#ד: ["It does not release blood in the inner. Some say regarding a thick piece as explained siman 69 s.k. 19 it is permitted — here the inner is not considered one piece with the outer — investigate; and according to what is explained siman 69 s.k. 4 that even b'dieved forbidden if birds were not salted inside and outside and cooked — here too l'chatchila must salt outer inside and outside and inner on all sides, rinse well, and fill; and otherwise forbidden for pot even b'dieved — as Acharonim wrote:"]
siftei-kohen.1#ה: ["And all this applies when this filling has only meat alone, etc. — implies from Rav's words that specifically meat alone is permitted, but if there are eggs with meat, even with unsalted meat — its law is like eggs alone; and so Or Zarua and Acharonim — no distinction; and so Leket Yosher concludes explicitly, unlike Maharshal who holds filling eggs with unsalted meat is all like meat filling — no reason at all; and it also appears from Rav that if there is sixty in the filling against the prohibition in the filling everything is permitted, for he wrote plainly its law is as if cooked in a pot — all this explained above siman 73 — see there:"]
siftei-kohen.1#ו: ["And even b'dieved one should forbid if both were not salted. Meaning: in filling with eggs one should forbid b'dieved if the outer meat and also the inner with the eggs were not salted — as in the s.k. before this:"]

turei-zahav.1#א: And even if the outer was salted. Explanation: and it exuded all its blood; Beit Yosef wrote unlike Hagahot Maimoniyot who forbids when outer salted and not inner because outer is not busy to exude; and Tur HaChadash general rule 9 ruled like Hagahot Maimoniyot and so Mordechai; but when inner salted and not outer — all agree permitted because fire draws blood. Rashal wrote chapter of Chullin siman 29 that when both salted, even if did not remain, or inner salted and did not remain and outer not salted — all permitted; prohibition only when outer salted and did not remain and inner not salted — then inner alone is forbidden.
turei-zahav.1#ב: For as it absorbs, etc. — and it is not comparable to meat that was salted and fell into gravy which is forbidden — there exudation is after time of absorption.
turei-zahav.1#ג: Outer alone. Explanation: and rinse them.
turei-zahav.1#ד: It does not release blood in the inner. Explanation: Rashal — and these are his words: it does not release blood inside, meaning of the inner side of the outer itself, even though inner was salted, end of his words; and though language does not imply so, one should be concerned for his words for practical halachah; and it is not comparable to what he ruled siman 69 permitting b'dieved when salted on one side — here worse since filling inside seals on all sides.
turei-zahav.1#ה: If both were not salted. Explanation: full salting, each alone until fit for pot in all its laws if meat with eggs in filling. (This belongs to Tur.) See Tur: it is written to distinguish between animal, etc.; Beit Yosef wondered we do not find this language in Scripture, etc. — all this can be answered in one answer; and we further analyze Tur's language "it is written" whereas in many places Tur begins with verses without saying "it is written" — nevertheless here he said "it is written" — and though not a great precision, incidentally we answer within our words. Rather Rav saw the derashah Beit Yosef mentioned only that derashah is found in two places — end of Shemini and end of Kedoshim — and Rashi explained in both verses; but certainly the primary derashah is from the verse at end of Kedoshim "and you shall distinguish," etc.; and what Rashi explained in Shemini is another matter — see there; primary learning is from Kedoshim; in Shemini he also explained similarly; but primary intention of "it is written" is the law Rashi explained that one must know and be expert — not to bring verse language only; and what Beit Yosef wondered why not bring verse "between the animal that may be eaten" — that comes for itself as we said; and Darkei Moshe also wrote this is only Rav's language not the verses.

baer-heitev.1#א: Salted. Explanation: remained for time of salting and rinsed — then it does not exude even gravy — nevertheless permitted; and Taz wrote some say meat salted and fell into gravy is forbidden — there exudation after absorption.
baer-heitev.1#ב: Inner. Shach wrote Rav's view: even if inner salted and remained for time of salting it does not absorb from outer — fire draws; Shach disagrees — when inner remained and outer unsalted or did not remain — inner forbidden since regarding inner we do not say as it absorbs so it releases; but if inner not salted forbidden only when outer salted and did not remain — then inner absorbs before roasting and does not exit again even by roasting; and since inside, ein hana'asur does not apply; but when inner equals outer — both salted and remained, or both unsalted, or both salted and did not remain — permitted; when inner unsalted and outer salted, remained, rinsed — obviously permitted; if inner salted and did not remain and outer salted, remained, rinsed — outer forbidden for it absorbs from inner before roasting (Peri Chadash disagrees — we are lenient in all cases like Shach; Mordechai proof I explained agrees Shach; Peleti challenged from spit — I answered utensils are different).
baer-heitev.1#ג: Alone. Explanation: and rinse after salting each alone (otherwise meat cooked without final rinsing — Shach).
baer-heitev.1#ד: Releases. Some say thick piece permitted — here inner not one piece with outer; per siman 69 s.k. 4 even b'dieved forbidden if not salted inside and outside — l'chatchila salt outer inside and outside and inner all sides, rinse, fill; otherwise pot forbidden even b'dieved (Magen Avraham in name of Gaon Maharash forbade zefek remaining with food inside bird — meat absorbed blood at salting; same gizzard salted with contents inside and cooked — forbidden; not like mere filling absorbing blood in eye).
baer-heitev.1#ה: In the inner. Rashal: does not release blood inside of inner side of outer even if inner salted. Not like siman 69 permitting b'dieved one-sided salting — here worse since filling seals all sides. Taz responsum 46: forbidden to roast unsalted with onion on spit even b'dieved; Peri Chadash lenient l'chatchila where custom permits; Mekor Baruch siman 36 permits plainly — where Maharshal forbade, be stringent.
baer-heitev.1#ו: Meat. Shach: implies only meat alone permitted; eggs with meat even unsalted — law like eggs alone, unlike Maharshal; also if sixty in filling against prohibition in filling — all permitted, law as cooked in pot — siman 73.
baer-heitev.1#ז: Both. Meaning: in egg filling forbid b'dieved if outer and inner with eggs not salted.

beer-hagolah.1#_: Statement of Rava, Psachim daf 74; and Rif and Rosh wrote it in chapter Gid HaNasheh.

beur-hagra.1#א: That was not salted. Tosafot there s.v. hai mulayta, etc.; and Rashi follows his view that roasting requires some salting — we do not hold thus as written siman 76.
beur-hagra.1#ב: If for roasting, etc. — and for cooling, etc. — for pot ein hana'asur does not apply; therefore Gemara fixed it regarding roasting the Pesach. Rif.
beur-hagra.1#ג: And even if, etc. Tosafot there s.v. kevolei. And one may learn, etc.
beur-hagra.1#ד: But if, etc. Rosh in chapter Gid HaNasheh — otherwise certainly forbidden for pot since not salted — see there.
beur-hagra.1#ה: And all this b'dieved, etc. — as his view written siman 76 seif 2 that practice l'chatchila like Rashi that even for roasting requires salting.
beur-hagra.1#ו: Unsalted meat, etc. — as above; and even if salted, etc.

kaf-hachayim.1#_: (1) [Seif 1] Birds or kids filled with unsalted meat. Explanation: bird or kid stuffed with ground unsalted meat. Beit Yosef in name of Rosh. Leket Yosher.

kereti.1#א: And even if, etc. — and it exuded all its gravy — coating of bar goose also exudes all its gravy.
kereti.1#ב: And all the more so if inner salted. Shach challenged; he holds if inner salted and remained and outer unsalted or did not remain — inner forbidden; if outer unsalted only forbidden when outer salted and did not remain — inner absorbs before outer; not like siman 70; when both equal — permitted; if inner salted not remained and outer salted remained rinsed — outer forbidden; see Peleti I wrote Peri Chadash and Magen Avraham challenged Shach from Mordechai — I explained Mordechai agrees Shach; Peleti challenged from spit — utensils different, not as sticky as food; hagalah proves for vessel not food; nevertheless do not innovate Shach's law; proofs from ein machzikin dam — see there.
kereti.1#ג: Eggs — even with meat, eggs impede and require sixty against prohibition as cooking law; all this for dissenters; for Rambam and Rashba no difference between eggs and meat; stam they said filling permitted — rely on great loss.

nekudot-hakesef.1#_: (Siman 77 Taz s.k. 1) And Beit Yosef wrote. This is not as Shach s.k. 2 wrote — see there.

peleti.1#_: And all the more so if inner salted, etc. — Rav Shach challenged; his view: if inner salted and remained and outer not salted — treifah; if outer salted and did not remain — obviously treifah; Peri Chadach and Magen Avraham challenged from Mordechai chapter 25 — no substance; Mordechai needs explanation — both not salted, or both for pot and did not remain for roasting; if outer salted not remained and inner not salted — perhaps inner forbidden as not busy, absorbs outer blood; both not salted — as it absorbs so it releases applies; proof from putting gizzards inside — perhaps there both salted; according to my explanation both salted for pot without remaining — cannot dismiss proof; appears Mordechai words difficult — what challenge if not salted forbidden, what proof from gizzards; perhaps there not salted at all — permitted all agree; perhaps salting was full for pot and remained — cannot establish forbidden case in Pesach; Mordechai clear, supports Shach — Magen Avraham did not delve; Peleti challenged from spit in roast — vessel different; Mordechai: concern absorbs from piece before exuding via salting — no salting for vessels; Shach challenged from Rambam birds roasted and salted though meat inside live — implies salting first; Rambam perhaps like siman 70 rinsed meat draws out; Rama forbids here; Rambam perhaps when placed rinsed meat to draw blood — fire does not impede; Rama ruled forbid; can squeeze out — forbidden; Rambam not chanan in morning issurim; perhaps squeeze permitted. Proof ein machzikin dam in gizzards — if outer not salted Mordechai holds gizzards have gravy; if not salted per Shach forbidden as inner like salted rinsed; most proofs do not hold like Shach — do not innovate dispute. If outer salted not remained and inner not salted — Mordechai forbidden from doubt; forced ein hana'asur siman 70 — fire absorbs more; Shach comparison reversed not forced; outer has more fire power expels what absorbed from inner; if coated bar goose was salted — permitted; why make dispute without clear proof — investigate.

rabbi-akiva-eiger-yd.1#_: (Siman 77 Shach s.k. 2) Or already exuded all its gravy. See above siman 73 Shach s.k. 14; requires further study.

yad-ephraim.1#_: It does not release. Avodat HaTaharah and hagahah brought Magen Avraham on zefek or gizzard remaining with food — see there; see Kenesset Yisrael siman 27 disagrees and permits; Meshiv Tzedek siman 69 s.k. 14 also inclined to permit — for practical halachah requires further study; seems forbid only in great loss; see above siman 75 s.k. 8. If piece of animal hide fell in stew — Levushi Serad forbids until sixty like meat cooked without salting — blood in hide; Taz there disagrees — I say do not forbid hide blood at all — Scripture speaks only of flesh blood; Tosafot Chullin 64 — rabbinic decree on fowl blood; but do not decree hide blood because of meat blood — clear to me; we forbid fowl hide because of blood — fowl hide is soft and eaten like meat; not animal hide — not called meat, no blood prohibition.
